Morrison et al. (2017) · Controlled monolayer CdS shell growth

Cadmium Bis(phenyldithiocarbamate) as a Nanocrystal Shell-Growth Precursor

Calynn E. Morrison; Fudong Wang; Nigam P. Rath; Brian M. Wieliczka; Richard A. Loomis; William E. Buhro · 2017 · 10.1021/acs.inorgchem.7b01711 ↗

Evidence typeliterature protocol
Reviewsource reviewed
Download record JSON ↓

Complete supplied 10-page main article and matched 17-page SI read and independently audited. Separate canonical/reader, molecular and apparatus audits passed. Two shell-growth routes, eight supporting procedures and eight observation contexts remain distinct. Printed conflicts and unresolved specimen joins are preserved. Precursor crystal coordinates are not CdSe/CdS product coordinates. No new training task or exact structure–recipe pair is admitted.

02

Synthesis protocolOrdered operations, material dependencies and stage-specific conditions

01
workup

Remove excess amine using three precipitate-retaining washes

Add toluene to the 0.512 g starting dispersion aliquot, centrifuge, discard the supernatant, and retain the belt precipitate. Repeat twice for three total washes; the dispersion mass is not a dry CdSe mass. Missing fields for this phase: core concentration in0.512g dispersion.

02
synthesis

Heat the washed belts in the THF precursor solution

Suspend the washed belts in the Cd(PTC)2/THF solution and heat at 66 °C. The source reports 3 h as ideal and 1.0–1.5 times an estimated monolayer requirement, but does not supply the core-concentration or surface-area calculation. Missing fields for this phase: core mass/surface estimate.
